textureKeys.doc: feature size in px: how big the grains, cells or lines are
how strong the layer is, 0 to 1 (more than 1 over-drives it)
noise contrast: 1 is as generated, higher is harsher
noise cut-off: only values above it show (glitter uses a high one)
draw thin lines where the noise crosses the threshold, instead of a plain cut: veins, rings, contours
noise detail layers, 1 is smooth, 5 is rough
a different random pattern with the same look
stretch noise features along x and y, e.g. stretch 40 1 for wood grain
bump height: how deep the relief looks
bump light direction in degrees
direction of lines and patterns, in degrees
line or grid-line width in px
dot size as a fraction of the cell (plaid: how wide the bands are as a fraction of the repeat)
how soft the edges of dots and lines are
milliseconds per shimmer step (film-grain flicker); 0 is still
noise flavour: fractal is clouds, turbulence is veins
how the layer mixes with what is under it
the main colour (dark end of noise, ink of lines and dots)
the second colour (light end of noise, background cell of patterns)
rings generator: how strongly the growth rings arch into a cathedral figure, 0 is straight grain
rings generator: how much each ring wobbles along its length
rings generator: fine fibre and pore streaks between the rings
rings generator: how many knots in one tile (the pattern repeats, so keep it small)
rings generator: lay it out as planks this many px tall, with a seam and a slightly different board each

mirror every other tile, so each edge meets its own reflection: no seam, and the repeat is twice as far apart. x mirrors left to right, y top to bottom, both (the default) does both. Works on the image-based textures (noise, bump, rings, waves, hex).
starfield and terrazzo: how many stars or chips in a tile, 1 is normal
swap the two colours

glowKeys.doc: the light colour (default: the element's text colour)
how far the glow reaches, in px
milliseconds for one breath in and out; 0 is steady
how deep the pulse goes, 0 to 1
random flicker, like a flame: 0 is steady, 1 is wild
a different random flicker with the same look
texture(grain scale 2): break the light up with a texture
keep animating even when the visitor prefers reduced motion
let the light spill out of a parent that clips (overflow: hidden, auto, scroll). Without it the aura is cut at that edge, like the element itself

the shape the light follows: follow (the default: the element's clip-path or rounded corners), box, round, pill, diamond, triangle, hexagon, octagon, pentagon, star, star4, star6, cross, heart, drop, bolt, alpha (an or 's visible pixels), or polygon(50% 0, 100% 50%, 50% 100%, 0 50%)
light inside the edge (a rim) instead of outside it
that many beams of light from the middle, slowly turning (see spin)
rays turn this many degrees a second (default 10); on particles, how fast each one tumbles
rings that spread out from the shape and fade, one every this many milliseconds
only the rays and ripples, without the soft halo
keep emitting even when the element cannot be seen (opacity 0, display: none, visibility: hidden, on it or an ancestor): for an invisible anchor that smoke or sparks come out of
the z-index of the layer this light is drawn on: `z 5` puts it under a hill with z-index 10. It meets elements in the page's root stacking context

particleKeys.doc: colours over a particle's life: color #ff0 -> #f60 -> transparent
how many particles are alive at once
diameter in px: size 4, or size 10 4 (start and end of a random range)
how long one lives, in ms: life 900, or life 600 1200
px per second: speed 60, or speed 30 90
where they head: up, down, left, right, out, in, or degrees (-90 is up)
how wide the fan of directions is, in degrees
px/s squared; negative pulls up (flames), positive down (snow)
air resistance: how fast particles slow down
random sideways wobble, px/s
where they are born: edge or outline (along the element's real outline, see around), bottom, top, left, right, center, corners, thumb (range sliders)
circle, spark, square, ring, star, flame, smoke, line, heart, diamond, triangle, plus, drop, bubble, snowflake, confetti or leaf
size at the end of life as a multiple of the start: 0.2 shrinks, 3 swells
add makes overlapping particles brighter, normal just stacks them
soft glowing particles that add light
draw only outside the element's box, as if the element hid them
a different random pattern with the same look
texture(grain): grainy particles
keep animating even when the visitor prefers reduced motion
let the particles leave a parent that clips (overflow: hidden, auto, scroll). Without it they are cut at that edge
the shape `from edge` and `from outline` follow: follow (the default), box, round, pill, diamond, triangle, hexagon, octagon, pentagon, star, star4, star6, cross, heart, drop, bolt, or polygon(...)
each particle takes ONE of the colours (confetti) instead of fading through them
how fast each particle tumbles, in degrees a second (random direction)
a sideways push, px/s squared; negative pushes left
the particles circle the middle of the element, this many degrees a second
keep emitting even when the element cannot be seen (opacity 0, display: none, visibility: hidden, on it or an ancestor): for an invisible anchor that smoke or sparks come out of
the z-index of the layer these particles are drawn on: `z 5` puts them under a hill with z-index 10. It meets elements in the page's root stacking context

sliderClauses.form: shape circle | square | diamond | pill | bar

glassWords.doc: a number: how many px to blur what is behind the element (default 16)
saturate <n>: colour boost for what shows through, 1 is unchanged (default 1.5)
bright <n>: brightness of what shows through, 1 is unchanged
tint <color> | tint none: the milky layer on top (default: a faint wash of the text colour)

tiltWords.doc: a number: the largest tilt in degrees (default 8)
lift <n>: scale while the pointer is over it, e.g. 1.04
perspective <px>: how strong the 3D depth looks (default 900)
speed <0.05 to 1>: how quickly it follows (default 0.18)
invert: tilt away from the pointer instead of toward it
glare: also keep --dssl-gx and --dssl-gy (0% to 100%) pointing at the pointer, for your own highlight
